text_nodes.text: The pens are counted. The AI isn't.
West Texas A&M received $9.75 million from USDA for a research feedlot near Canyon. The A&M System calls it the largest federal award in WT's history. The yard and the cattle are drawn to illustrate.

text_nodes.text: USDA pays half. The match pays the rest.

A required dollar for dollar match brings the project to $19.5 million. The A&M System puts in $4.875 million. The Texas Cattle Feeders Association, donors and other sources match it. Each section is drawn to stand for one $4.875 million share.
The feedlot goes up beside WT's 2,393-acre ranch

The ranch lies about seven miles east of Canyon and was given to WT in 1971. Canyon ranchers Mike and Gary Kuhlman gave 42.84 acres beside it in 2024. Each is drawn as a square of its own area, not its real shape or exact place.
EACH GRID SQUARE IS ONE MILE ON A SIDE

text_nodes.text: 90 research pens paired with 45 commercial ones
That is 135 pens in all. Each commercial-scale pen here faces two small research pens across a feed alley. The layout and pen sizes are drawn to illustrate the count.

text_nodes.text: Ground is broken. Four facilities are planned.

Ground was broken in November 2025. Plans call for a precision beef cattle handling facility, a veterinary care and research hospital, an advanced technology feed and production center and a metabolism and physiology center. The section and stakes are drawn to illustrate.

text_nodes.text: Texas's large feedlots held more cattle than Nebraska's or Kansas's

On September 1st USDA estimated 2.5 million cattle on feed in Texas's large feedlots, 2.47 million in Nebraska and 2.32 million in Kansas. Texas held 22 percent of the 11.16 million nationwide. Each steer is drawn to stand for 500 thousand head.
